principalStates.label: Capable
principalStates.description: The individual is alive and presumed to have capacity to make and revoke financial, health-care, and estate-planning decisions.

principalStates.label: Incapacitated
principalStates.description: The individual is alive but found (by the method each act specifies) to lack capacity, or, for financial purposes, is missing, detained, or unable to return to the U.S.

principalStates.label: Deceased
principalStates.description: The individual has died; lifetime agencies end and post-death roles (anatomical gift priority, small-estate successor, named executor) come into play.

principalStates.label: Estate administration
principalStates.description: A personal representative has been appointed and letters issued, so estate administration has commenced (UPC §3-103).

principalStates.label: Closed
principalStates.description: The estate is settled by court order or closing statement, and the personal representative's appointment has terminated.

If it names no one, a physician (or licensed psychologist) can certify impairment, or a lawyer, judge or government official can certify that the principal is missing or detained.

conditions: If the POA names a successor agent, the successor may act once all predecessors have resigned, died, become incapacitated, are not qualified or decline (§111(b)); the POA itself continues
Resignation is by notice to the principal and, if the principal is incapacitated, to the conservator/guardian and coagent or successor, or others listed (§118)

transitions.event: An action is filed for dissolution/annulment of the agent's marriage to the principal, or their legal separation
conditions: Applies only where the agent is the principal's spouse
Default only: the POA may provide otherwise

transitions.event: POA provides that it terminates, or its purpose is accomplished
conditions: Lapse of time alone does not terminate authority unless the POA so provides (§110(c))

transitions.event: Court appoints a conservator/guardian of the principal's estate
conditions: Agent becomes accountable to the fiduciary as well as the principal
[Bracketed text] POA not terminated; authority continues unless the court limits, suspends, or terminates it

transitions.event: Court limits or suspends the agent's authority
conditions: On petition by persons listed in §116(a), including a conservator/guardian

transitions.event: Court terminates the agent's authority

roles.name: Agent under power of attorney for health care
roles.summary: An individual appointed in a power of attorney for health care to make health-care decisions when the principal cannot. Under UHCDA (2023) decision-making power always 'springs' on a finding of lack of capacity, and only the health-information power may start at once. The 1993 Act let the document make the agent's authority effective immediately.

assigned.event: Individual signs power of attorney for health care (2023: in a record with one qualifying adult witness; 1993: signed writing)

starts.event: Finding of lack of capacity under §4(b) or by a court (2023). 1993: primary physician's determination unless the directive says otherwise, or immediately if the POA so specifies

ends.event: Principal found to have regained capacity (power ceases; may resume)
Revocation by principal; spouse-agent divorce/separation events; disqualification

Principal's death: neither UHCDA text expressly addresses this; no post-death powers (autopsy, disposition of remains) are granted. Any post-death anatomical-gift authority comes from Revised UAGA §9(a)(1)

states.label: No power of attorney for health care
Agent appointed; principal has capacity (agent may hold immediate health-information access if the POA so provides)
Principal found to lack capacity; agent may make health-care decisions
Power ceased because principal objected to the incapacity finding (2023); may resume
Appointment revoked, disqualified, or otherwise ended

transitions.event: Individual creates power of attorney for health care
conditions: 2023: record signed by the individual and an adult witness who is not the agent, the agent's spouse/domestic partner/cohabitant, or (for nursing-home residents) facility owner/operator/employee/contractor; witness may be present by real-time audio-visual or, in some cases, audio (§8(d)-(e))
1993: writing signed by principal; no witness required (§2(b) and comment)
Presumption of capacity to make the appointment (2023 §4(a); 1993 §11(b))

transitions.event: POA provides that agent's health-information power commences on appointment
conditions: 2023: applies only to the power to request, receive, examine, copy, and consent to disclosure of health information (§18(b)); decision-making still requires incapacity finding (§18 cmt.)

transitions.event: Individual found to lack capacity (2023 Act)
conditions: Finding under §4(b): contemporaneous examination by physician, licensed psychologist, [PA/APRN/social worker with training], or responsible health-care professional in urgent situations when those are unavailable; documented in signed record with cause, nature, extent, probable duration
Finder may not be a family member, cohabitant, or the surrogate or surrogate's family (§4(c))
Or a court finding (§18(a); judicial review by clear and convincing evidence, §6)
Individual and surrogate must be informed (§5(a)-(b))

transitions.event: Determination that principal lacks capacity (1993 Act)
conditions: Made by primary physician unless the written directive specifies otherwise (§2(d))
If the POA expressly so provides, authority may be effective immediately or on another event (§2(c) and comment); in that case this transition is skipped
Person then authorized to decide has the patient's rights to health-care information unless the directive says otherwise (§8)

transitions.event: Individual objects to the §4(b) finding (orally, in a record, or by other act)
conditions: 2023 only; individual must be treated as having capacity unless an exception in §5(d) applies (e.g., urgent condition, court finding)

transitions.event: Finding confirmed by a second qualified, independent finder or by a court
conditions: A second finding cannot rebut capacity where the individual requests life-sustaining treatment and the finding would be used to withhold/withdraw it (§5(e))

transitions.event: Individual later found to have capacity
conditions: 2023: presumption of capacity restored if condition no longer exists or responsible professional has good cause (§4(d))
1993: authority ceases on primary physician's determination of recovered capacity (§2(c)-(d))

transitions.event: Individual revokes appointment
conditions: 2023: any act clearly indicating intent, including oral statement to a health-care professional; not available if a court found (or a confirmed §4(b) finding shows) the individual lacks capacity to revoke (§15(a)-(b))
1993: revocation of agent designation only by signed writing or personally informing supervising provider (§3(a))

transitions.event: Individual revokes appointment while capable
Spouse-agent: divorce/annulment/separation event
conditions: 2023: petition filed (not dismissed), decree issued, separation agreed in a record, or abandonment >1 year, unless directive provides otherwise (§15(d))
1993: decree of annulment, divorce, dissolution, or legal separation, unless decree or POA specifies otherwise (§3(d))

transitions.event: Agent disqualified
conditions: 2023: court finds agent poses danger, or agent is owner/operator/employee/contractor of the nursing home where the individual resides, unless family/cohabitant (§8(b))
1993: owner/operator/employee of residential long-term care institution where principal receives care, unless related (§2(b))

transitions.event: Original agent unavailable, resigns, dies, or is disqualified; alternate agent acts
conditions: 2023 default: alternate has same authority while the original agent is not reasonably available, or permanently once all predecessors resigned/died/disqualified (§20(c))

transitions.event: Court appointing a guardian expressly orders revocation of the directive
conditions: Absent such an order, the agent's decision prevails over the guardian's (2023 §22(b); 1993 §6(b))

transitions.event: Principal dies
conditions: Not expressly stated in UHCDA 1993 or 2023; inferred because a 'health-care decision' concerns the individual's own health care
Neither Act grants post-death authority (autopsy, disposition of remains). Anatomical-gift authority after death is under Revised UAGA §9(a)(1), see role anatomical-gift-agent

roles.name: Default health-care surrogate
roles.summary: A person who can make health-care decisions for an individual who lacks capacity and has no available agent or guardian. The law picks this person from a priority list, or the individual can name them without signing a power of attorney.

assigned.event: Individual identifies a surrogate other than in a POA (2023 §12(b)(1); 1993: by personally informing supervising provider), or by operation of the priority list

starts.event: Individual found to lack capacity and no agent/authorized guardian appointed or reasonably available; highest-priority reasonably available, non-disqualified person assumes authority

ends.event: Capacity regained, or agent/guardian becomes available
Disqualification or bypass by responsible health-care professional
Death of individual (not expressly addressed)

states.label: No identified or eligible surrogate
Individual identified by the patient, or eligible by priority class; no authority while patient has capacity
Has assumed authority to make health-care decisions
Power ceased due to patient's objection to incapacity finding (2023)
Disqualified, bypassed, superseded, or ended

transitions.event: Individual identifies an adult to decide if the individual cannot
conditions: 2023: other than in a POA for health care; highest priority class (§12(b)(1)); may also be expressed in a health-care instruction (§7(a)(5))
1993: by personally informing the supervising health-care provider (§5(b))

transitions.event: Individual found to lack capacity; surrogate assumes authority (2023)
conditions: No agent or guardian authorized for health care appointed or reasonably available (§12(a))

Priority (unless directive says otherwise): (1) adult identified by individual; (2) spouse [or domestic partner] unless divorce/separation petition, decree, agreement, or abandonment >1 yr; (3) adult child or parent; (4) cohabitant; (5) adult sibling; (6) adult grandchild or grandparent; (7) adult who routinely assisted with supported decision making in prior 6 months; (8) adult stepchild actively parented; (9) adult who showed special care and concern and knows the individual's values (§12(b))
Responsible professional may require declaration under penalty of perjury (§12(c))
Majority of highest class controls on disagreement; even split resolved by other law (§13)
Power commences on §4(b) or court finding (§18(a))
May not make a decision that other state law bars a guardian from making, or allows only with specific court authorization (§19(b))

transitions.event: Primary physician determines patient lacks capacity; surrogate acts (1993)
conditions: No agent or guardian appointed or reasonably available (§5(a))
Priority: designee; then spouse unless legally separated, adult child, parent, adult sibling; then adult with special care and concern (§5(b)-(c))
Must notify family members in §5(b) (§5(d)); even split disqualifies the class and all lower classes (§5(e))

transitions.event: Patient objects to §4(b) finding
conditions: 2023 only

transitions.event: Finding confirmed by second independent finder or court
Patient found to have capacity
Agent or guardian authorized for health care is appointed or becomes reasonably available
conditions: Default surrogate authority exists only in their absence (§12(a); 1993 §5(a))

transitions.event: Responsible professional recognizes next in priority because surrogate is unwilling/unable to comply with §17 duties or fails to do so timely
Surrogate disqualified
conditions: By the patient in a signed record or verbal/nonverbal communication, effective even if patient lacks capacity for an advance directive (§14(a))
Court finds danger; nursing-home owner/operator/employee/contractor unless family; refusal to give timely declaration (§14(b))
1993: patient may disqualify by signed writing or informing supervising provider (§5(h))

transitions.event: Individual revokes the designation of a default surrogate
Patient dies
conditions: Not expressly stated in either Act; inferred from scope of health-care decision authority

roles.name: Guardian for an adult (personal affairs)
roles.summary: A person a court appoints to make decisions about an adult's personal affairs (where they live, health care and the like). The court must find by clear-and-convincing evidence that less restrictive alternatives will not work. UGCOPAA (2017) replaces the 1997 UGPPA, and the 2019 UPC still contains the UGPPA as Article V.

assigned.event: Nomination by respondent (e.g., in a POA or health-care directive) is considered for priority, but only a court appoints

starts.event: Court order of appointment, then filing of acceptance and issuance of letters of office

ends.event: Court terminates guardianship and restores rights (prima facie evidence standard)
Adult dies (stated in official comment)
Guardian dies, is removed, or court approves resignation

states.label: No proceeding
Person nominated by the respondent (nomination has priority weight only)
Petition for guardianship pending
Emergency guardian appointed: only powers in the order, not more than [60] days (one extension)
Appointment ordered; letters not yet issued (acceptance not filed), or successor appointed to serve on a future event
Letters issued; guardian exercising powers granted (full or limited)
Authority suspended while a temporary substitute guardian serves
Guardianship or this guardian's appointment ended

transitions.event: Respondent nominates a guardian (e.g., in a POA or advance health-care directive)
conditions: Priority order: guardian acting in another jurisdiction; respondent's nominee (most recent, including in a POA); health-care agent; spouse [or domestic partner]; family member or other person with special care and concern; court may depart in respondent's best interest (§309)

transitions.event: Person interested in the adult's welfare (including the adult) petitions
conditions: Predecessor: UGPPA (1982/1997), which built on UPC Article V (1969); UGCOPAA replaces the 1997 UGPPA (Prefatory Note)
The UPC text as amended through 2019 still carries the UGPPA as Article V (§5-101)

transitions.event: Petition filed where a nominee exists
Court appoints emergency guardian
conditions: Likely to prevent substantial harm; no other person appears to have authority and willingness to act; reason to believe §301 basis exists
Attorney appointed immediately; without-notice appointment requires notice within 48 hours and hearing within [5] days
Not a determination that a §301 basis exists

transitions.event: Emergency authority expires ([60] days, extendable once) or court removes the emergency guardian
Court orders appointment after notice and hearing
conditions: Clear-and-convincing evidence that respondent cannot meet essential requirements for health, safety, or self-care even with supports, and needs cannot be met by a protective arrangement or less restrictive alternative (§301(a))
Only powers necessitated by demonstrated needs; full guardianship only with findings that limited guardianship would not meet needs; order states retained rights to vote and marry (§§301(b), 310)

transitions.event: Guardian files acceptance; court issues letters of office
conditions: Limitations on powers must be stated on the letters (§108(c))
Default powers (except as limited by order) include establishing dwelling, consenting to health care, applying for benefits, receiving health information (§314)
Guardian may revoke or refuse to comply with an advance health-care directive only if the court expressly orders; agent's decision prevails unless court orders otherwise (UHCDA 2023 §22)

transitions.event: Court appoints successor guardian to serve immediately or when a designated event occurs (e.g., death of parent-guardian)
conditions: Successor may act when the event occurs and it complies with §108; has predecessor's powers unless court provides otherwise
Note: a 'standby guardian' under the Act (§207) exists only for minors

transitions.event: Court modifies powers (expands or limits) and issues new letters
Court appoints temporary substitute guardian (≤6 months) while removal is pending or guardian not effectively performing
Temporary substitute's authority ends without removal of the guardian
conditions: Inferred: §125(c) suspends existing guardian's authority only 'for as long as' the substitute has authority

transitions.event: Court removes guardian for failure to perform duties or good cause and appoints successor (per §309 priorities)
Court removes guardian after temporary substitution
Guardian petitions to resign; effective on court approval
Guardian dies
conditions: Liability for prior acts and duty to account survive (§112(c))

transitions.event: Court terminates guardianship (restoration of rights)
conditions: Petition by adult, guardian, or interested person; on prima facie evidence court shall terminate unless §301 basis is proven
Adult has right to choose an attorney

transitions.event: Adult subject to guardianship dies
conditions: Stated in official comment, not black-letter text of §319
UGCOPAA grants no express post-death winding-up authority to a guardian of the person (contrast conservator §§427, 431(k))

roles.name: Conservator (property and financial affairs)
roles.summary: A person a court appoints to manage an adult's property or financial affairs. When the adult dies, the conservatorship terminates. The conservator then winds it up by filing a final report and delivering the estate to the decedent's estate, and a bracketed option lets the conservator ask for personal-representative powers.

assigned.event: Respondent's nomination (including in a POA for finances) and agent status give priority; court appoints

starts.event: Court order, then acceptance and any bond filed and letters of office issued

ends.event: Adult dies: conservatorship terminates; final report, distribution to estate, discharge
Court terminates (basis no longer exists); property passes to the individual
Conservator dies, is removed, or resignation approved

states.label: No proceeding
Person nominated by respondent
Petition pending
Emergency conservator: only powers in order, not more than [60] days (one extension)
Appointment ordered; awaiting acceptance and bond/asset-protection compliance
Letters issued; managing conservatorship estate
Authority suspended while a temporary substitute conservator serves
Individual has died: conservator files final report, preserves and distributes estate, awaits discharge
Discharged or appointment ended

transitions.event: Respondent nominates a conservator (e.g., in a POA)
conditions: Priority: conservator in another jurisdiction; respondent's nominee (most recent, incl. in POA for finances); agent under POA for finances; spouse [or domestic partner]; family member or other person with special care and concern (§410)

transitions.event: Petition filed
Petition filed where nominee exists
Court appoints emergency conservator
conditions: Likely to prevent substantial and irreparable harm to property/financial interests; no one else with authority and willingness; reason to believe §401 basis exists; hearing within [5] days

transitions.event: Emergency authority expires or court removes emergency conservator
Court orders appointment
conditions: Adult: clear-and-convincing evidence that adult cannot manage property due to decision-making limitation even with supports, or is missing, detained, or unable to return to the U.S.; appointment necessary to avoid harm/dissipation or to provide support; no less restrictive alternative (§401(b))
Limited conservatorship order must specify property and powers (§411(d))

transitions.event: Conservator files acceptance and any required bond; letters issued
conditions: Existing agent under a financial POA becomes accountable to conservator; authority continues unless court limits (UPOAA §108(b))
Digital assets: access to the extent RUFADAA or court order provides (§418(l); RUFADAA §14)
May exercise settlor's power to revoke/amend revocable trust only with court approval (UTC §602(f))

transitions.event: Court appoints successor conservator to serve immediately or on a designated event
Temporary substitute conservator appointed (≤6 months)
Temporary substitute's authority ends without removal
conditions: Inferred from 'for as long as' wording of §125(c)

transitions.event: Conservator dies, is removed, or court approves resignation
Court terminates conservatorship (basis no longer exists / best interest)
conditions: Prima facie evidence standard; property passes to the individual; final report and discharge (§431(f), (j))

transitions.event: Adult subject to conservatorship dies
conditions: Conservatorship terminates at death (§431(b))
Deliver any will in possession to court and inform named personal representative (§427(a))
May take reasonable measures to preserve the estate until distribution (§431(k))

transitions.event: [Bracketed option] 40 days after death with no PR appointed or pending, conservator applies to exercise PR powers
conditions: Court may grant if no objection; letters endorsed; has effect of PR appointment under UPC §3-308 and Parts 6-10 of Article III (§427(b)-(c))

transitions.event: Court approves final report; conservator distributes to decedent's estate or as ordered; final order of discharge

roles.name: Personal representative named in will (executor)
roles.summary: The person a will nominates to administer the decedent's estate. Being named gives no general power until a court or Registrar appoints them, they qualify, and letters issue. Once appointed, their powers relate back to earlier acts that benefited the estate.

starts.event: Appointment (informal: ≥120 hours after death, will probated), qualification (bond/acceptance), issuance of letters; powers relate back

ends.event: Order closing estate (formal)
One year after closing statement with no pending proceedings
Removal, resignation (effective on successor), PR death/conservator, change of testacy

states.label: No will nomination
Named in will; before appointment may only carry out decedent's written instructions on body, funeral and burial
Appointment ordered by Registrar/court; must qualify (bond if required + statement of acceptance) before letters
Letters issued; administration commenced; full PR powers
Removal petition pending: may act only to account, correct maladministration, or preserve estate
Closing statement filed; appointment continues for one year
Appointment terminated

transitions.event: Will nominates executor (or confers power to nominate)
conditions: Person with priority under probated will is first in priority (§3-203(a)(1))
No PR powers before appointment (§3-103)

transitions.event: Testator dies; named executor carries out written instructions about body, funeral, and burial
conditions: Permitted before appointment (§3-701)

transitions.event: Application for informal appointment granted (or formal appointment order)
conditions: Informal: at least 120 hours after death; will formally or informally probated; applicant has priority (§§3-307, 3-308)
Non-resident decedent: delay until 30 days after death unless exceptions (§3-307(a))
Generally no appointment proceeding more than 3 years after death, with exceptions (§3-108)
Must be at least [21] and not found unsuitable (§3-203(f))

transitions.event: Files any required bond and statement of acceptance; letters issued
conditions: Administration commences on issuance of letters (§3-103)
Duties and powers commence on appointment; powers relate back to beneficial prior acts; may ratify others' proper acts (§3-701)
Fiduciary held to trustee standards; broad transaction powers (§§3-703, 3-715)
Digital assets: catalogue/non-content by default; content only with user consent or court direction (RUFADAA §§7-8)

transitions.event: Nominee renounces or is disqualified
conditions: Renunciation by writing filed with the court (§3-203(c)); disqualification (§3-203(f))

transitions.event: Interested person petitions for removal; PR receives notice
conditions: After notice PR shall not act except to account, correct maladministration, or preserve the estate, unless court orders otherwise (§3-611(a))

transitions.event: Court orders removal for cause
conditions: Cause includes best interests of estate, misrepresentation, disregard of court order, incapacity, mismanagement (§3-611(b))
After termination, may still act to protect the estate and deliver assets to successor (§3-608)

transitions.event: PR files written resignation after ≥15 days' notice to interested persons
conditions: Effective only on appointment and qualification of a successor and delivery of assets (§3-610(c))

transitions.event: PR dies or a conservator is appointed for PR's estate
conditions: PR's own representative must protect the estate until a successor or special administrator is appointed (§3-609); special administrator may be appointed (§3-614)

transitions.event: Later will probated / probate vacated and a person entitled under the new testacy status is appointed
Court order of complete settlement (§3-1001) or settlement under informally probated will (§3-1002)
conditions: Petition not entertained until time for presenting pre-death claims has expired

transitions.event: PR files verified closing statement ≥6 months after original appointment
conditions: Creditor-claim period expired; estate fully administered and distributed; copies and account sent to distributees and known unpaid claimants (§3-1003(a))

transitions.event: One year after closing statement with no proceedings pending, appointment terminates

roles.name: Personal representative in intestacy (administrator)
roles.summary: The personal representative of an estate with no will, or where no one named in a will serves. They are appointed from a statutory priority list: surviving spouse, then other heirs, then any creditor 45 days after death.

assigned.event: Priority arises at death by relationship (spouse, heirs) or by nomination from a person with priority

starts.event: Appointment (informal ≥120 hours after death), qualification, letters; powers relate back

ends.event: Order closing estate
One year after closing statement with no pending proceedings
Removal, resignation, PR death/conservator, later will probated

states.label: Decedent alive or no eligible applicant
Has statutory priority or has been nominated by persons with priority; no powers yet
Appointment ordered by Registrar/court; must qualify (bond if required + statement of acceptance) before letters
Letters issued; administration commenced; full PR powers
Removal petition pending: may act only to account, correct maladministration, or preserve estate
Closing statement filed; appointment continues for one year
Appointment terminated

transitions.event: Decedent dies intestate (or will nominee does not serve); person holds priority
conditions: Order when no will-based priority: surviving spouse who is devisee; other devisees; surviving spouse; other heirs; any creditor 45 days after death (§3-203(a))
Persons with priority (a)(2)-(5) may nominate a qualified person; co-equal priority holders must concur (§3-203(c))
Conservator (or guardian) of a protected heir may exercise that person's right to nominate (§3-203(d))

transitions.event: Informal or formal appointment
conditions: Informal: ≥120 hours after death; applicant has priority (§§3-307, 3-308(a)(7))
Appointment of someone without priority only in formal proceedings after those with priority fail to act (§3-203(e))
3-year ultimate time limit with exceptions (§3-108)

transitions.event: Special administrator appointed to protect estate before general PR
conditions: Informally on application of interested person when necessary to protect the estate (§3-614)

transitions.event: Bond (if required) and acceptance filed; letters issued
conditions: Powers relate back (§3-701)

transitions.event: Renounces in writing filed with court
Interested person petitions for removal; PR receives notice
conditions: After notice PR shall not act except to account, correct maladministration, or preserve the estate, unless court orders otherwise (§3-611(a))

transitions.event: Court orders removal for cause
conditions: Cause includes best interests of estate, misrepresentation, disregard of court order, incapacity, mismanagement (§3-611(b))
After termination, may still act to protect the estate and deliver assets to successor (§3-608)

transitions.event: PR files written resignation after ≥15 days' notice to interested persons
conditions: Effective only on appointment and qualification of a successor and delivery of assets (§3-610(c))

transitions.event: PR dies or a conservator is appointed for PR's estate
conditions: PR's own representative must protect the estate until a successor or special administrator is appointed (§3-609); special administrator may be appointed (§3-614)

transitions.event: Later will probated / probate vacated and a person entitled under the new testacy status is appointed
Court order of complete settlement (§3-1001) or settlement under informally probated will (§3-1002)
conditions: Petition not entertained until time for presenting pre-death claims has expired

transitions.event: PR files verified closing statement ≥6 months after original appointment
conditions: Creditor-claim period expired; estate fully administered and distributed; copies and account sent to distributees and known unpaid claimants (§3-1003(a))

transitions.event: One year after closing statement with no proceedings pending, appointment terminates

roles.name: Successor collecting personal property by small-estate affidavit
roles.summary: For a small estate, a person entitled to the decedent's personal property can collect it by affidavit 30 days after death, without court appointment. Anyone who pays or delivers property to them is protected as if they had dealt with a personal representative.

assigned.event: Death; person is a successor entitled to payment or delivery

starts.event: 30 days after death, presents affidavit (entire estate net of liens ≤ $25,000; no PR application pending or granted)

ends.event: Property paid/delivered; affiant remains answerable to any PR or person with superior right
PR application filed or granted (affidavit condition fails)

states.label: Decedent alive or no entitled successor
Entitled successor; waiting period (30 days) running
Affidavit presented; holders must pay or deliver
Collection complete or superseded by PR appointment

transitions.event: Decedent dies; person is successor entitled to property
Affidavit presented to holder of property/debtor/transfer agent
conditions: 30 days elapsed since death
Value of entire estate wherever located, less liens and encumbrances, ≤ $25,000
No application or petition for PR appointment pending or granted in any jurisdiction
Affiant entitled to payment or delivery
No court involvement required
RUFADAA [bracketed] accepts a small-estate affidavit in lieu of letters for PR digital-asset requests (§§7(3), 8(3))

transitions.event: Holder refuses to pay/deliver
conditions: Property may be recovered in a proceeding brought by or for persons entitled (§3-1202)

transitions.event: Payment/delivery made
conditions: Payor discharged as if dealing with a PR; recipient answerable to any PR or person with superior right (§3-1202)

transitions.event: PR application/petition filed or granted
conditions: Affidavit condition (a)(3) no longer satisfiable

roles.name: Successor trustee of a revocable (living) trust
roles.summary: A person named in the trust to take over when the trusteeship becomes vacant. When that happens depends mainly on the trust's own terms (for example, the settlor-trustee's incapacity as the trust defines it). By default the UTC creates a vacancy when a trustee dies, resigns, is removed, or gets a guardian or conservator. The successor serves only after accepting.

assigned.event: Settlor names successor trustee in the trust terms

starts.event: Vacancy occurs per trust terms (e.g., incapacity as defined by the trust) or by default on death, resignation, removal, or appointment of guardian/conservator for an individual trustee; successor accepts

ends.event: Trust terminates (e.g., after distribution following settlor's death) and trustee distributes
Successor resigns, is removed, dies, or gets a guardian/conservator
Settlor with capacity revokes/amends trust to remove successor

states.label: No successor named
Named in trust terms as successor; no duties before acceptance
Accepted trusteeship; administering trust
Rejected, resigned, removed, died, or trust terminated

transitions.event: Settlor names successor in trust instrument
conditions: Capacity to create/amend revocable trust is same as to make a will (§601)
Trust terms generally prevail over UTC defaults (§105)

transitions.event: Vacancy occurs and successor accepts
conditions: Trigger: whatever the trust terms specify (commonly settlor-trustee's incapacity as defined in the instrument), or by default: trustee dies, resigns, is removed or disqualified, or a [guardian]/[conservator] is appointed for an individual trustee (§704(a))
UTC itself contains no incapacity-certification procedure for trustees; the trust terms control (§105)
Acceptance: substantial compliance with trust's method, or by accepting delivery of trust property, exercising powers, or otherwise indicating acceptance (§701(a))
Before accepting, may act to preserve trust property if rejection is sent within a reasonable time, and may inspect property (§701(c))

transitions.event: Designated successor rejects, or does not accept within reasonable time after knowing of designation (deemed rejection)
conditions: Vacancy then filled by next designated successor, unanimous agreement of qualified beneficiaries, or court (§704(c))

transitions.event: Settlor loses capacity while trust revocable
conditions: [Bracketed] trustee's duties owed exclusively to settlor only while settlor has capacity to revoke; after incapacity beneficiaries' rights no longer subject to settlor control (§603(b) & cmt.)
Agent may exercise settlor's revocation/amendment powers only if expressly authorized by trust or POA; conservator/guardian only with court approval (§602(e)-(f))

transitions.event: Settlor dies; trust becomes irrevocable
conditions: Within 60 days after learning the trust became irrevocable, notify qualified beneficiaries of trust's existence, settlor identity, right to copy of instrument and to reports (§813(b)(3))
Within 60 days after accepting, notify qualified beneficiaries of acceptance and contact details (§813(b)(2))
Digital assets: trustee access under RUFADAA §§11-13

transitions.event: Settlor (with capacity) amends/revokes trust to remove successor
Trustee resigns on ≥30 days' notice to qualified beneficiaries, settlor if living, and cotrustees, or with court approval
Court removes trustee (serious breach, unfitness, changed circumstances, etc.)
Trustee dies or a guardian/conservator is appointed for trustee
conditions: Former trustee's PR, conservator or guardian may send the report to qualified beneficiaries (§813(c))

transitions.event: Trust terminates under its terms and trustee distributes
conditions: Trustee shall proceed expeditiously to distribute, subject to reasonable reserve (§817(b))
Role ends on completion of wind-up; exact end point not specified in black-letter text

roles.name: Designated recipient under a custodian's online tool
roles.summary: A person the account holder picks through a service provider's own online tool (separate from the terms of service) to receive or manage digital assets. If the tool lets the user change or delete the choice at any time, the direction overrides a contrary will, trust, or power of attorney. The designated recipient is not held to fiduciary standards.

assigned.event: User designates recipient via custodian's online tool

starts.event: Future event set by the online tool, such as the user's death or incapacity (the Act defers to the tool; no statutory trigger), then request to custodian

ends.event: User modifies or deletes the direction
Custodian discloses or terminates account (≤[60] days after required information) (end point not specified)

states.label: No online-tool direction
Named in online tool; direction revocable by user
Triggering event per online tool occurred; recipient may request disclosure or account termination
Direction deleted/modified, or disclosure/termination completed

transitions.event: User directs custodian via online tool to disclose (or not) some or all digital assets, including content, to designated recipient
conditions: Online tool must be distinct from the terms-of-service agreement (§2(16))
If the tool allows modification/deletion at all times, it overrides contrary will, trust, POA, or other record (§4(a))
Overrides contrary TOS provision not requiring distinct affirmative act (§4(c))
Priority: online tool, then will/trust/POA/other record, then TOS, then Act's defaults (§4 cmt.)

transitions.event: User modifies or deletes the direction
Future event specified in the online tool occurs (e.g., death or incapacity)
conditions: The Act does not define the trigger: the comment describes the tool as naming someone to manage assets 'after the occurrence of a future event, such as the user's death or incapacity'

transitions.event: Recipient requests disclosure or account termination
conditions: Custodian may grant full access, partial access, or a copy of assets the user could have accessed (§6(a)); may charge reasonable fee (§6(b)); need not disclose assets the user deleted (§6(c)); may seek court order if segregation is unduly burdensome (§6(d))

Custodian must comply within [60] days after receiving required information, else recipient may seek court order (§16(a)); custodian may deny if aware of lawful access after the request (§16(d)); may notify user (§16(c))
Authority subject to TOS except as §4 provides, copyright and other law; may not impersonate user (§15(b)); no expanded rights beyond user's (§5(b))
Not held to fiduciary standard of conduct (§2 cmt.)

transitions.event: Disclosure or account termination completed
conditions: Act does not specify when the designated recipient's role ends

roles.name: Fiduciary seeking access to digital assets (PR, conservator, agent, trustee)
roles.summary: RUFADAA gives no new fiduciary status of its own. It sets out when an existing personal representative, conservator, agent, or trustee can get a digital-asset catalogue or content from a custodian. By default, content of electronic communications needs the user's consent (or, for a personal representative, a court direction). A conservator also needs a court order after a chance for a hearing.

assigned.event: Underlying fiduciary status arises under other law (POA, trust, court appointment, letters or small-estate affidavit)

starts.event: Written request with required documents; custodian must comply within [60] days

ends.event: Underlying authority ends (e.g., agent's POA ends at principal's death, conservatorship ends, PR appointment terminates)
Estate closed

states.label: No fiduciary
Holds fiduciary status under other law; no request made
Request submitted with required documents; custodian obligated to comply within [60] days
Underlying fiduciary authority ended, or request fulfilled

transitions.event: Person becomes PR, conservator, agent, or trustee under other law
conditions: Act applies to fiduciaries under instruments whenever executed, and to custodians if user resided in the state (§3)
Access may be modified/eliminated by user, federal law, or TOS if user gave no §4 direction (§5(c))

transitions.event: Personal representative requests catalogue and non-content digital assets of deceased user
conditions: Default: disclosed unless user prohibited or court directs otherwise

Documents: written request; [certified] death certificate; [certified] letters, small-estate affidavit, or court order; on custodian's request, account identifier, evidence linking account, affidavit that disclosure is reasonably necessary, or court finding (§8)

transitions.event: Personal representative requests content of electronic communications
conditions: Only if deceased user consented or a court directs
Also requires copy of will/trust/POA/other record evidencing consent unless user used an online tool (§7(4))

transitions.event: Agent requests content of principal's electronic communications
conditions: POA must expressly grant authority over content; unless principal or court directs otherwise
Documents: written request; original/copy of POA; agent's certification under penalty of perjury that POA is in effect (§9)

transitions.event: Agent requests catalogue and non-content assets
conditions: Agent with specific authority over digital assets or general authority; unless court, principal, or POA provides otherwise (§10)

transitions.event: Trustee requests digital assets held in trust
conditions: Trustee as original user: all assets incl. content (§11)
Trustee not original user: content requires trust instrument/certification including consent (§12); catalogue and other assets with certified trust copy/certification (§13)

transitions.event: Conservator obtains court order granting access after opportunity for hearing, then requests
conditions: Custodian discloses catalogue and non-content assets only (no content provision for conservators) (§14(a)-(b))
Conservator with general authority may request suspension/termination of account for good cause with certified court order (§14(c))

transitions.event: Custodian responds
conditions: Full/partial access or copy at custodian's discretion; reasonable charge; deleted assets need not be disclosed; undue-burden court options (§6)
Must comply within [60] days of receiving required information; court order available; custodian may require court order with specified findings; good-faith immunity (§16)

transitions.event: Fiduciary requests termination of user's account
conditions: Written request with death certificate (if deceased) and [certified] letters/small-estate affidavit/court order/POA/trust (§15(g))
Fiduciary acting within scope is authorized user for computer-fraud laws; duties of care, loyalty, confidentiality apply; may not impersonate user (§15)

transitions.event: Underlying fiduciary authority ends
conditions: E.g., agent's POA terminates at principal's death (UPOAA §110(a)(1)); agent must certify POA is in effect (§9(3), §10(3))
Authority limited by scope of the fiduciary's duties (§15(b)(3))

roles.name: Agent authorized to make an anatomical gift
roles.summary: A health-care agent, or a person a signed record expressly authorizes, can make an anatomical gift during the donor's life unless the document forbids it. After death, the person who was the decedent's agent at death has first priority to make a gift. The donor's own gift or refusal bars others.

assigned.event: Principal appoints health-care agent or signs record expressly authorizing anatomical gift

starts.event: During donor's life: agent may make gift by donor card/record/registry (unless prohibited)

ends.event: After death: first-priority authority exercised or barred; revocation by others ineffective after incision/invasive procedures begin
Donor's unrevoked refusal or own gift bars the agent

states.label: No agent
Agent under health-care POA or record expressly authorizing gift
Donor alive; agent has made (and may amend or revoke) a gift under §4(2)
Donor has died; agent at time of death holds first priority under §9(a)(1) while reasonably available
Barred, gift made and acted upon, or authority lapsed

transitions.event: Principal signs health-care POA, or another signed record expressly authorizing agent to make an anatomical gift
conditions: Both UHCDA optional forms include an organ-donation part (1993 §4 Part 3; 2023 §11 Part D), but the gift's effect and priority are governed by the Revised UAGA

transitions.event: Agent makes anatomical gift during donor's life
conditions: Unless the POA or other record prohibits it (§4(2))
By donor card or other signed record, or authorizing registry entry (§5(b))
Barred if donor made an unrevoked refusal (§7(d)) or donor's own gift/amendment (absent contrary indication) (§8(a))
Where a directive exists, medical-suitability measures may not be withheld unless directive expressly provides otherwise (§21)

transitions.event: Agent amends or revokes the gift the agent made
conditions: By signed record, later document of gift, or destruction/cancellation with intent (§6)
Cannot alter a donor's own gift (§8(a))

transitions.event: Donor dies with agent still authorized
conditions: Class 1 priority: agent at time of death who could have made a gift under §4(2) immediately before death; then spouse, adult children, parents, adult siblings, adult grandchildren, grandparents, adult with special care and concern, guardian of the person, others with authority to dispose of body (§9(a))
Procurement organization must search for persons with priority (§14(g))

transitions.event: Donor dies after agent made a gift under §4
conditions: Another person may not make, amend, or revoke that gift under §10 (§8(c))

transitions.event: Agent makes gift of decedent's body or part
conditions: By signed document of gift, or oral communication electronically recorded or reduced to a signed record (§10(a))
Must be reasonably available; lower classes may not act if a prior class is reasonably available (§9(c))
Not permitted if barred by §7 or §8 (§9(d))

transitions.event: Donor's own unrevoked refusal or gift bars others
Agent not reasonably available; next class may act
